summary: Amherst is one of a handful of US colleges — and one of very few liberal-arts colleges — that admits international students need-blind and meets their full need. Its aid never includes loans.
covers: Need-blind admission for international students: your aid request is not considered.
100% of calculated financial need met for admitted international students who apply for aid.
No-loan aid: offers contain only grants, scholarships and student employment.
eligibility: First-year applicants from any country applying to Amherst College.
Aid is based on calculated need from your family's financial documents.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Common Application or QuestBridge with Amherst's requirements.
Choose Early Decision (binding, 9 November 2026) or Regular Decision (5 January 2027).
Submit your financial aid application with the admission application.
Ask for an application fee waiver if the fee is a barrier.
watch_out: Early Decision is binding — only use it if Amherst is your clear first choice and the aid estimate works for you.
Amherst's intake is small (under 500 first-years), so admission is very competitive.
Being need-blind for internationals is rare; strong applicants who need full aid should put Amherst on their list.

faq.q: Will asking for aid affect my chances?
faq.a: No. Amherst is need-blind for international applicants, meets 100% of calculated need, and its aid offers contain no loans.

faq.q: Do I need the SAT or ACT?
faq.a: No. Test scores are optional for every applicant, including international students.

Not at first — it is outside the initial aid budget. But if you receive Amherst aid and use the college's health plan, the $3,627 cost is added to your budget and covered by a Health Insurance Scholarship.
